name: Triglyceride Deposit Cardiomyovasculopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Triglyceride Deposit Cardiomyovasculopathy

criteria.description: Presence of triglyceride accumulation in myocardial and vascular tissues confirmed by biopsy
Cardiac MRI showing diffuse myocardial lipid infiltration and impaired myocardial function
Identification of pathogenic mutations in PNPLA2 or related lipid metabolism genes
Presence of progressive heart failure symptoms with preserved coronary arteries
Elevated serum triglycerides and abnormal lipid profiles

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus either characteristic imaging findings or genetic mutation identification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other cardiomyopathies and metabolic disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive congestive heart failure with preserved coronary arteries

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion due to cardiac dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Chest discomfort without coronary artery disease
Mild hepatomegaly due to lipid accumulation
searchTerms: slightly enlarged liver from fat buildup
mild liver enlargement due to lipids

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to cardiac embolism
searchTerms: neurological problems due to heart clot

rare.symptomName: Muscle weakness due to systemic lipid storage
searchTerms: progressive muscle loss due to lipid buildup
weak muscles caused by fat deposits

laboratory: Elevated serum triglycerides and abnormal lipid panels
Normal or mildly elevated cardiac enzymes
imaging: Cardiac MRI showing diffuse myocardial lipid infiltration
Coronary angiography showing absence of obstructive coronary artery disease
genetic: Mutations in PNPLA2 gene (encoding adipose triglyceride lipase)
Variants in other lipid metabolism-related genes
other: Histopathological evidence of triglyceride deposits in myocardial and vascular tissues
Absence of significant atherosclerosis despite cardiac symptoms

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including renal and neurological
Primarily elevated triglycerides without myocardial lipid infiltration
Muscle biopsy showing lipid droplets in myocytes

redFlags: Rapidly progressive heart failure symptoms despite normal coronary arteries
Refractory arrhythmias in young adults without structural heart disease
Histological evidence of myocardial triglyceride accumulation
references: Nishino I, et al. Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy: a novel form of cardiomyopathy. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2017;69(12):1536-1547.
Yamaguchi S, et al. Clinical and genetic features of triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy. Circ J. 2019;83(5):1020-1027.
